# Realtime Location Tracker

> A high-performance, real-time geolocation tracking system built with Node.js, Express, Socket.IO, and Leaflet.js.

## Overview

The Realtime Location Tracker is a lightweight web application designed to capture real-time spatial updates via HTML5 Geolocation APIs and transmit coordinate shifts instantaneously using WebSockets (`Socket.IO`). Connected client locations are plotted dynamically on an interactive map rendered via `Leaflet.js` and `OpenStreetMap`.

## Key Features

- **Realtime Bidirectional Communication:** Low-latency WebSocket connections via Socket.IO for streaming spatial coordinates.
- **Client-Side Geolocation:** Uses `navigator.geolocation.watchPosition` for continuous device tracking.
- **Interactive Mapping:** Interactive map visualization powered by Leaflet.js with customized marker management.
- **Dynamic Session Handling:** Automatic marker spawning when users connect and marker removal on socket disconnect.

## Tech Stack

### Backend & Middleware
- **Runtime:** Node.js
- **Framework:** Express.js (HTTP server hosting & static asset delivery)
- **Realtime Layer:** Socket.IO (Server instance)
- **View Engine:** EJS (Embedded JavaScript)

### Frontend & Client Tools
- **Mapping Library:** Leaflet.js
- **Tiles Provider:** OpenStreetMap Tile Layer (`https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`)
- **Realtime Client:** Socket.IO Client SDK
- **Geolocation API:** Browser-native HTML5 Geolocation API

## Architecture & Data Flow

1. **Connection Initialization:**
   - Client accesses the HTTP server via Express.
   - Server renders the EJS template containing the map canvas and client scripts.
   - Client establishes a persistent WebSocket connection to the Socket.IO server.

2. **Position Tracking & Emission:**
   - Client requests high-accuracy location tracking (`enableHighAccuracy: true`).
   - On position change, client emits a `send-location` event containing `{ latitude, longitude }`.

3. **Broadcasting & Rendering:**
   - Server listens for `send-location` and broadcasts `{ id: socket.id, latitude, longitude }` to all connected clients (`io.emit`).
   - Every client receives the coordinates and updates/creates the corresponding marker in the `Leaflet` layer map.

4. **Disconnection Lifecycle:**
   - On connection termination, server emits `user-disconnected` containing the `socket.id`.
   - Clients capture this event and remove the corresponding marker layer from the map.

## File Structure

```text
Realtime-Location-Tracker/
├── public/
│   ├── js/
│   │   └── script.js      # Client-side Socket.IO & Leaflet map logic
│   └── css/
│       └── style.css       # Map viewport styling and DOM layout
├── views/
│   └── index.ejs          # HTML structure loading Socket.IO, Leaflet, and scripts
├── app.js                 # Express server & Socket.IO initialization
├── package.json           # Dependencies and runtime scripts
└── README.md              # Documentation

```

## Setup & Running Instructions

### Prerequisites

-   Node.js (v14+ recommended)
    
      
    
-   npm or yarn
    
      
    

### Installation

Bash

```
# Clone the repository
git clone [https://github.com/mahmud-r-farhan/Realtime-Location-Tracker.git](https://github.com/mahmud-r-farhan/Realtime-Location-Tracker.git)

# Navigate into project directory
cd Realtime-Location-Tracker

# Install dependencies
npm install

```

### Execution

Bash

```
# Start the application
npm start
# or using nodemon for development
npx nodemon app.js

```

By default, the server runs on `http://localhost:3000`.

  

## Code Conventions & Standards

-   **Asynchronous Events:** Rely on Socket.IO event-driven architecture rather than polling.
    
      
    
-   **Memory Safety:** Ensure markers are mapped to `socket.id` dictionary keys on the client to allow `O(1)` deletion and prevent client-side memory leaks on long-running sessions.
    
      
    
-   **Client Configuration:** Set `timeout` and `maximumAge` parameters on `watchPosition` to ensure location freshness while conserving client system resources.
    

```
